text:
Arjun R: FYI ran a targeted FP8 canary against long-dialog prompts and observed a different failure mode than the usual repetition. posting notes here so we don't duplicate work.
Nina L: what happened?
Arjun R: gist: toward the tail of some conversations (2k+ tokens) a handful of attention heads spike scales, but different heads across requests. the model drifts to a low-entropy, high-certainty state and keeps reusing a short KV window. not a classic top1 repeat but a tonal collapse.
Evan T: do you have a log snippet?
Arjun R: yes — sample (anonymized):
```
[2026-01-08T18:11:03Z] token=2110 rolling_entropy=0.32 head10_scale=12.3 head23_scale=0.9 kv_overlap=0.67
[2026-01-08T18:11:03Z] token=2111 topk_entropy=0.21 deg_score=0.82 quant_scale_global=3.9
[2026-01-08T18:11:03Z] token=2112 reply_fragment="the same phrase repeated" kv_overlap=0.69
```
Kira M: interesting — sounds like miscalibrated per-head outliers that the global quant scale doesn't catch. we've seen headwise heavy tails before but not so transient.
Nina L: hypothesis: calibration sampling didn't include long-prefix activations or rare prompt shapes; scale estimator gets biased and occasional heads explode.
Evan T: possible runtime mitigations?
Arjun R: prototype idea: soft-clamp per-head scales at runtime using a sigmoid limiter when head_scale > threshold; don't fully fallback precision, just clip extreme scales and zero out tiny KV reuse if kv_overlap > 0.6 for a bad window.
Kira M: soft-clamp could preserve most perf while avoiding full INT8/FP16 fallback. but clipping changes distribution — we need offline eval to ensure no new hallucinations.
Nina L: alternative: per-request precision-hint header. client can opt into a more conservative path for long-dialog workloads (disable aggressive fp8 calibration, or use per-layer int8 for last N layers).
Evan T: runtime detection options:
- rolling_entropy < 0.45 for M tokens -> soft-clamp + disable KV reuse for K tokens
- per-request deg_score > 0.75 -> route rest of request to conservative path (per-layer int8 / fp16 tail)
Arjun R: tradeoffs: soft-clamp is lower cost but risk subtle quality shifts. conservative route is safer correctness-wise but ~1.8-2.3x token cost. Need per-tenant budgets.
SRE-Bot: note: introducing soft-clamp as a feature flag during canary is low-risk. if canary fallback rate > 0.5% we should pause and alert billing.
Billing-Bot: tagging: if conservative route used in prod >1% of requests, estimated monthly cost +23%.
Kira M: proposed plan:
1) implement server-side soft-clamp + kv_overlap breaker behind feature flag (Evan)
2) instrument head-scale histograms, per-request deg_score, and kv_overlap sampling (Nina)
3) add a precision-hint header and per-tenant fallback budget in config (Arjun + Product)
4) run a 72h canary with sampled payloads and offline eval on a held-out long-dialog set (include automatic A/B against pure FP16 path)
Nina L: metrics to monitor: fp8_softclamp_incidents, avg_degradation_score, user-visible coherence regressions from eval harness, fallback_rate_per_tenant.
Evan T: I'll spin up a PR with the clamp math (sigmoid with tunable knee and max_clip) and a no-op path so we can A/B easily.
Arjun R: also adding a small safeguard: if soft-clamp doesn't reduce deg_score within 10 tokens, escalate to full precision fallback for that request.
Kira M: good. documentation note: add guidance for customers running very long chains (>=2k) to set precision-hint when they expect coherent long-form threads.
SRE-Bot: scheduling: canary deploy with clamp flag enabled tomorrow at 09:00 UTC, sampling on, alerts muted for canary window.
Arjun R: opened ticket RDW-5420 (fp8-tail-drift-softclamp). will post the canary link and sampled traces there. thanks everyone. :wave:
